column1: # Mount roots judged with symlinks resolved: the ONE list of cases every reader
# (the shared bash rule in bin/* and install.sh, rclone-mount, the TUI, the
# panel) is tested against. A root that passes valid_root (roots.tsv) is still
# refused when the path it resolves to (realpath -m: missing components are
# fine, a dangling link is followed as far as it goes) is the home or inside
# it, the home taken both as written (normalised as in homes.tsv) and
# resolved. Why: programs that crawl the home (file search, indexers, backup
# tools) would follow the link into the cloud drive and download it.
# Each case builds a fresh tree under a temp dir T, with HOME=T/home:
#   - T/home is created as a directory unless a step makes it a link;
#   - <setup> is ";"-separated steps, applied in order, or "-" for none:

# link:

= ln -s T/

(the parent of T/

created first);
#                      <t> starting with "@/" stands for T/<rest>, any other
#   - <root> is relative to T (the root judged is T/<root>).
# T itself must be a plain path that passes valid_root (no spaces).
